feature: A picked shape in an icon says where it sits and how big it is
summary: Pick a shape in an icon and a tag above it reads its place and size in units, 9, 10 · 6 × 3, or center 12, 8 · d 8 for a circle. It keeps up with a move or a resize, so you no longer look at the panel to check a shape landed where you meant.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A 24 unit icon frame at 800%. Walk: a-picked-icon-shape-names-its-place-walk.

evaluate: Does the tag land where your eye already is, with the rotate knob beside it?
Is it right that the pill under a drag goes away in an icon, leaving this tag as the one reading?
With a shape near the top of an icon, does the tag crowding the frame's name bother you?
rough: The mock centres the tag above the shape; the app puts it above and to the left, because the rotate knob and the mode chip stand in that spot and the mock draws neither. Settled by UX-PATTERNS §D12, the placement law: never cover the subject, and flip or move before anything else.
A shape near the top of an icon puts the tag right up against the frame's name label. It does not cover the shape or a grip, and it can touch that label.
With a shape filling the view there is nowhere clear, so no tag shows and the panel carries the numbers.
The tag shows in Size only. Skew and 3D keep their own reading under the frame.
A move with the Grid off can stop on a half unit: the box caught the icon's centre line and the tag honestly read 9, 10.5.
